question: Which HS2 product chapters had the largest decline in Luxembourg's imports between 2007 and 2008 financial crisis?

limitations.message: Values are in current euros (nominal), not adjusted for price changes.
4.9 % of this value is confidential at full product detail (masked codes); it is shown as a separate 'Confidential' slice, never dropped.

sql:
SELECT
  year,
  hs2 AS key,
  flow,
  SUM(value_eur) AS value_eur,
  SUM(qty_kg) AS qty_kg
FROM v_lu_trade_hs2
WHERE
  period >= CAST('2007-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND period < CAST('2009-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND flow = 'import'
  AND year IN (2007, 2008)
GROUP BY
  year,
  key,
  flow
ORDER BY
  year,
  value_eur DESC
LIMIT 10000
title: Largest changes by product group — imports 2007–2008

main.label: Inorganic chemicals; organic or inorganic compounds of precious metals, of rare-earth metals, of radioactive elements or of isotopes
Natural or cultured pearls, precious or semi-precious stones, precious metals, metals clad with precious metal, and articles thereof; imitation jewellery; coin

insight: The HS2 product chapters with the largest decline in Luxembourg's imports between 2007 and 2008 were Electrical machinery and equipment, which fell by 255.7 million euros, and Natural or cultured pearls, precious or semi-precious stones, precious metals, and related articles, which decreased by 80.2 million euros.

Overall, imports of Electrical machinery and equipment dropped from 1.45 billion euros in 2007 to 1.20 billion euros in 2008, and imports of precious stones and metals fell from 211.6 million euros to 131.5 million euros in the same period.
In contrast, imports of Mineral fuels and oils increased by 27.4%, and Machinery and mechanical appliances rose by 12.5% during the financial crisis.
These figures are nominal values in current euros and do not account for price changes over time.
Additionally, 4.9% of the import values are confidential at full product detail and are shown separately, which may affect the completeness of the data.
